based_on_test: RC4.3 physical test of 2026-10-04 17:27-17:35 (client report with SteamVR server, compositor and client logs; host report and driver log) and the user's report: what Sharpening is, doubt that foveated streaming worked, no eye-tracked settings or eye view, a sharper picture but jittery head and controller tracking, a pixelated in-headset quality line, no reconnecting card when the connection closed

findings.gpu: Integrated Radeon graphics at 800 MHz in every performance sample of the RC4.3 session (and both RC4.2 tests), 58-59 % busy, SoC about 15-18 W, mains connected and charging, performance level auto; SteamVR at 37.5 fps for 407 of 412 streaming seconds at 2560 per eye, host pose prediction about 96 ms
findings.compositor: vrserver: vrcompositor (pid 45499) disconnected at 17:35:12.88 with nothing in the compositor's own log; the VROSTBridge client exited -13 (SIGPIPE) at 17:35:21.7; vrserver stayed without a compositor until VROSTBridge closed SteamVR at 17:35:26
findings.foveation: Eye-tracked chosen with Calibrated eye tracking off: Balanced in use (host encoded 1792 x 1728 per eye instead of 2560 x 2560); RC4.3 hid the eye-tracked settings in that case
findings.overlay: the quality pill was drawn at about one image pixel per headset pixel and magnified by the compositor

scope: Held-back GPU (launcher/graphics_limit.py GpuClocks, launcher/performance_monitor.py max_sclk_mhz): the busiest GPU sampled every 5 s; median of the last 6 samples (3 needed) at >= 40 % busy and <= half the maximum clock marks it held back; the graphics warning names a power limit (TDP) or a fixed GPU clock first with the measured clock, maximum and power; in-headset line "GPU held at N MHz - raise the TDP limit"; live readout graphics.gpu on the client page, the Game Mode session card and the headset quality line; a bare maximum clock never creates a GPU row

SteamVR failure recovery on the client (launcher/app.py): exact vrserver/vrcompositor identities recorded at first video and checked every second (compositor gone with the server running, SteamVR gone, or a replacement compositor while frames are stalled; a replacement is adopted only after 4 s of unstalled frames); 2 checks in a row; nothing judged during a Stop, after a Stop was asked for or after SteamVR asked the client to quit; a non-zero native exit or a FATAL line (after up to 15 s) while SteamVR is lost restarts too; one automatic restart per 10 minutes on both PCs, a second failure stops with the explanation; Stops and Starts by hand win (counted, checked under the action lock); coredumpctl entry and kernel graphics lines logged for the report
Native client: SIGPIPE ignored (client and runtime probe); compositor frames stopped/advancing lines (also when frame timing is unavailable); stops when its companion command pipe closes

Game Mode lease helper started from one long-lived thread (launcher/game_mode.py PROCESS_STARTER): its PR_SET_PDEATHSIG follows the starting thread, so started from the Start request's thread (RC4.2, RC4.3) it would have been terminated, with the headset display, when Start returned; abandoned starts are ended

Fused frame pass (client/platform/linux/fused.comp): Catmull-Rom from 5 bilinear taps (renormalised), texels per output pixel from the analytic slope of the foveation inverse (client/device/conversion.hpp foveationDecompressSlope), sharpening taps only where detail = clamp(2 x texels - 1, 0, 1) > 0
Eye-tracked settings shown whenever Eye-tracked is chosen; system.foveation.eye_state (off-here, host-off, no-gaze, cpu, following) drives the page note and the Game Mode row

Headset cards and quality pill at up to 2x pixels per degree within the 2 MiB SetOverlayRaw budget (ui::fittedScale), overlay width divided by the scale, drawn once per change from the last fitting scale of their kind, shadow inset scaled
Sharpening described as separate from foveated encoding (pages and Game Mode)
Companion-only host repack over the RC4.3 payload
toolchain: Ubuntu 24.04, GCC 13.3.0, CMake 3.28.3 + Ninja 1.11.1, glslangValidator 15.1.0, Mesa lavapipe 25.2.8 (shader tests), PyInstaller 6.22.3 on Python 3.12.3, NSIS 3.09, Chromium (Playwright) for page renders

tests.native: 20/20 CTest suites. fused_shader_contracts: re-aimed detailed scene differs from the original by 0.639 levels (RC4.3 nine taps 0.724, RC4.2 two passes 2.212); analytic slope against finite differences within 1e-3 over region sizes 0.3-0.7, edge ratios 2-5 and shifts -0.6..0.6; texel density 1 in the centre and 1/7 at the outer edge (size 0.4, ratio 4). status_card_contracts: pill at 2x, fitted card scale above 1.2 within 2 MiB, softer edges at 2x
tests.shader_timing_lavapipe: 2048 x 1024, median of 11 interleaved runs: RC4.3 84.4 ms (96.7 with sharpening), RC4.4 65.6 ms (75.3); CPU-emulated, relative only
tests.desktop_ui: pass (eye_state notes, runtime_restart hint, GPU readout, one-pass and sharpening notes)
tests.page_renders: Chromium at 1280 and 390 px: client page with the held-back GPU warning and readout, eye-tracked settings with the eye-tracking-off note, the restart hint; host and client pages without page errors
tests.game_mode_renders: offscreen 1280 x 800: session card with the GPU text and readout, the restart text, Stream & headset with the Eye tracking is off row
tests.parent_death_signal: a child that sets PR_SET_PDEATHSIG is terminated when a short-lived starting thread exits and survives when started through PROCESS_STARTER (test_rc44)

package_checks: 55 client checks: ZIP CRC and payload SHA256SUMS; managed RC4.4 install over an RC4.3 install keeps settings; old version removed; desktop entries; native client and runtime probe labels 1.0.0-rc4.4; libvrosttext.so, convert.spv, reaim.spv and VROSTBridgeLease byte-identical to RC4.3, fused.spv/client/probe rebuilt; lease helper runs; ldd resolves; installed self-test; companion status (runtime_restart, graphics), page, fonts, artwork, stamped report, send-report outcome, quit; same-version repair; damaged-package refusal; uninstall keeps state

host payload: verified RC4.3 payload + RC4.4 companion and docs; every .exe/.dll/.pyd byte-identical to RC4.3; setup EXE built with NSIS 3.09 and its extracted payload re-verified against SHA256SUMS and identical to the repacked payload
independent_review: A separate review agent checked the RC4.4 changes in three rounds and reproduced its findings in a test harness: an automatic restart could override a Stop by hand; nothing ended an orphaned native client once SIGPIPE was ignored; the eye-tracking texts showed in a case they described wrongly; cards were drawn twice; restart messages outlived their session; a Stop just before the trigger, a compositor SteamVR replaced on its own, an unreadable SteamVR registry, a FATAL judged too early, a replacement adopted before its stall could show and an abandoned process start. All were fixed with tests; the shader math, the slope, the overlay scale arithmetic and the GPU sampling were confirmed.
known_limits: Why the integrated GPU stays at 800 MHz is not known from the logs: a TDP limit near 15 W or a fixed GPU clock; the RC4.4 readout and warning give the next test the numbers
The SteamVR compositor crash itself is not explained by its logs; RC4.4 records coredumpctl and kernel graphics lines when the user may read them
Nothing can be shown in the headset while SteamVR's compositor is down
The host driver (unchanged since RC4.1) still writes foveation centres every 5 s to its own log on the host PC; reports and the journal leave them out
remaining_validation: All RC4.4 behaviour on hardware (see RELEASE_1.0.0-rc4.4.md, How to test): the GPU readout and warning with a raised TDP limit, crisp headset text, the eye-tracking notes, Game Mode sessions with the Beyond 2e, and the restart if SteamVR fails again

RC4.3, RC4.2, RC4.1 and RC4 physical checks: host microphone, Game Mode settings and B, live eye view with calibrated eye tracking, Wi-Fi stalls, foveation on Index and Beyond 2e, wake/sleep, quick resume
